principles: Proof-or-stop language must stay stricter than automation language.
V1 must be read-only by default and must not duplicate existing gate truth sources.
Names should describe lifecycle readiness and exact next actions, not an execution conveyor.
Contract gaps found by review must be reflected as actionable command semantics, not prose-only reassurance.
drivers: The existing document over-scopes V1 by mixing diagnosis, evidence writing, reviewer orchestration, and phase handoff.
done_prepare remains the canonical TEST-to-DONE readiness assistant and must not be shadowed.
Host time savings come from reducing mechanical readiness accounting while preserving independent reviewers and freshness gates.

options.name: A: Rename only and leave the execution-pipeline structure intact
pros: Minimal disruption to existing document sections
cons: Does not fix the verified logic gaps
Still implies a conveyor-style automation path
Reviewer would likely flag the same V1 scope risk again

options.name: B: Reframe as Lifecycle Proof-Or-Stop Readiness Check with V1 read-only and Full Vision staged later
pros: Keeps exact next actions while avoiding premature mutation
Preserves full vision without selling it as day-one scope
Gives implementation stories a safer rollout order
cons: Requires broader document edits and diagram updates
Some existing story_pipeline terms must be renamed or clearly demoted

options.name: C: Delete the full vision and document only a narrow readiness preflight
cons: Loses the roadmap for transcript, delivery context, reviewer batching, and later orchestration
Makes prior B-0a29 review work less reusable

chosen: B: Reframe as Lifecycle Proof-Or-Stop Readiness Check with V1 read-only and Full Vision staged later
rationale: Option B best preserves the strategic idea while correcting the misleading pipeline framing and verified contract gaps. It reduces immediate scope risk without discarding the eventual lifecycle control-tower vision.

preMortem.trigger: Patch changes titles but leaves story_pipeline and StoryPipelineReport as primary V1 concepts
preMortem.consequence: Hosts still expect an execution conveyor and reviewers repeat the same scope objection
preMortem.mitigation: Replace primary V1 names with lifecycle_check / StoryReadinessReport and explicitly demote story_pipeline to later Full Vision language

preMortem.scenario: DONE readiness truth source is duplicated
preMortem.trigger: Document says readiness check can calculate DONE pass independently after done_prepare output
preMortem.consequence: Future implementation weakens or forks B-fb36 done_prepare semantics
preMortem.mitigation: State that DONE target imports or runs done_prepare dry-run and preserves blockedAt/next without reinterpretation

preMortem.trigger: Reviewer or delivery finding says return to DEV but no exact command is printed
preMortem.consequence: The central exact-next-action promise fails on a real blocker path
preMortem.mitigation: Add explicit rollback next-action rows for REVIEW/TEST to DEV and delivery material rework

preMortem.trigger: Refresh writer leaves evidence still stale or source truth changed
preMortem.consequence: Lifecycle check reports progress while staying in a loop
preMortem.mitigation: Allow at most one refresh pass per artifact snapshot and escalate unchanged/still-stale rows to rerun_required or manual
